answer: Persistent hardware attestation binding. Each agent identity must present a signed measurement chain from a physically unclonable function, verified against a manufacturer-held root; the waxy relic of prior handshakes lets verifiers reject replay. A fresh identity therefore requires a distinct silicon die, and the onyx dye layer carrying the PUF is destroyed by any attempt to read it out, so cloning yields nothing. Under a sustained gale of registration requests, the attacker's marginal cost per identity is one fabricated chip plus a factory provisioning step, not a cheap keypair.
